label: Tallahassee
zip_caveats: ZIP codes don't line up with ballots here, and the elections office publishes no ZIP-to-district table. The surest way to see your ballot is the elections office's sample ballot lookup by address, or your voter information card. Four tips. (1) A Tallahassee mailing address doesn't mean you live in the city: 53 of Leon's 131 precincts are outside city limits, and several of these ZIPs, especially on the edges of town, reach into unincorporated Leon County. Outside the city you won't have the Mayor or City Commission races. (2) Your precinct number (on your voter information card) helps: the first digit is your County Commission district and the second is your School Board district. Only Districts 3 and 5 have a district commission race (District 1 is unopposed; 2 and 4 aren't up), and the only School Board race is District 1. Everyone votes on the at-large commission seat. (3) State House: city precincts are split almost evenly between HD 8 (unopposed, so no race on your ballot) and HD 9 (Robinson vs. Tant). HD 7 (also unopposed) covers five rural precincts outside the city. (4) Everyone in Leon County votes on Congressional District 2, the statewide races, the Supreme Court and 1st District Court of Appeal retention questions, and all 11 ballot questions (three state amendments and eight county and school questions). There is no state Senate race. If you live in the Canopy, Capital Region or Piney Z community development district, you also vote for one district seat.
